document: LUCI Field Activation Guide — client version
purpose: Tailored step-by-step instructions to replace the generic 'Try it' callouts in the client FAG. Inline in the doc, no portal links.
methodology: Drafted from Mike's demo/training transcripts (Ameristar 2026-06-16, Angel of the Wind 2026-04-23) plus the functional activation guide copy doc. Every step is a DRAFT pending review by Mike Epstein or a LUCI FDE against the live product before it ships.

reviewRequired: Mike Epstein or a LUCI FDE must verify each workflow against the live product before it is published in the client FAG.
pipelineNote: Content (custom messages, promos, event graphics) lives in your digital signage CMS and reaches LUCI as a channel: signage player HDMI out → LUCI IP encoder → source in LUCI's list. That CMS→encoder→LUCI path is the same one-time setup behind most Marketing use cases, so it's written once here and referenced.

useCases.title: Push a message to every screen in under two minutes.
useCases.prerequisites: Your message exists as an image or short video, and a signage player is already wired into a LUCI encoder so its content shows up as a channel in LUCI. If not, do the one-time Setup first.
setup: In your digital signage CMS, open your media library and drag your message asset in (or pull it from a linked OneDrive/Canva). Set a validity end-date if the message is temporary so it auto-removes.
Create a playlist, add the message to it, and assign the playlist to a signage player. That player's output feeds a LUCI IP encoder, so the message now appears as a channel in LUCI's source list.
steps: Open LUCI in your browser from any device and log in.
On the property map, zoom out until every display on the floor is in view.
Use the lasso tool to select every TV on the property — or select just the zones you want to reach.
In the source list, pick the channel carrying your message. Every selected display flips to it immediately, live, with no ticket or call.
To drop back: set a revert time (e.g., 60 seconds) and the floor returns to its scheduled content on its own — or apply your 'normal' preset when you're done.
useCases.revert: Set a revert time in seconds on the push, or apply a return-to-normal preset. The floor drops back to scheduled content automatically.
assumptions: Lasso-then-select-source is the fastest path for a whole-property push (vs. building a preset). Confirm with Mike.
Revert time can be set on an ad-hoc push, not only on a scheduled preset. Confirm.
If the message must land on EVERY screen including the marquee/outdoor, those displays must be on the map (connected via encoder). Confirm scope.
useCases.reviewStatus: draft

useCases.title: Daypart your restaurant promotions to catch guests at the decision point.
useCases.prerequisites: Your dining spot asset exists and a signage player → LUCI encoder channel is set up for it (see UC1 Setup).
setup: Same one-time CMS setup as UC1: load the dining spot in your digital signage CMS, put it on a playlist, assign to a signage player so it appears as a channel in LUCI.
steps: In LUCI, open Presets and create a new preset (e.g., 'Pre-lunch dining spot').
Add the displays you want to reach — the floor-wide set, not just the screens near the restaurants. Select them on the map or from the venue list.
For each display in the preset, set its target to the dining spot channel.
Save the preset.
Open the Event Scheduler. Add the preset to the calendar in the hour before lunch (and a second entry in the hour before dinner). Set it to repeat daily, or pick specific days.
Set a revert time on each entry (e.g., one hour) so the floor drops back to regular rotation automatically — or schedule a 'normal' preset to follow it.
useCases.revert: Revert time on the preset, or a following 'normal' preset on the calendar.
assumptions: A single preset can target a floor-wide display set (vs. needing one per venue). Confirm.
Revert time is set per scheduled event. Confirm where the revert field lives — on the preset or on the scheduled event.
useCases.reviewStatus: draft

useCases.title: Give each zone its own bank of ads, its own schedule, and its own tone.
useCases.prerequisites: Each zone's bank of ads is loaded in your digital signage CMS and each is on its own signage player → LUCI encoder channel (one source per zone's content). If you want the tone to include lighting, confirm which zones have lighting controllable through LUCI (ETC Mosaic or Lutron).
setup: In your digital signage CMS, build each zone its own playlist — its bank of ads — on its own signage player (one player per zone that runs at the same time as another). Each player → LUCI encoder → its own channel in LUCI's source list, so the zone can be programmed independently.

If you want the tone to include lighting, confirm which zones have lighting controllable through LUCI (ETC Mosaic or Lutron). Lighting scenes recall per zone just like content channels, so a zone can dim or shift with its content.
steps: In LUCI, open the property map and pick the first zone (e.g., sports book). Select it from the venue list or tap its tag.
Select the displays in that zone, then in the source list pick that zone's content channel — its bank of ads. They flip immediately.

Build a preset for the zone that carries its displays, its content channel, and — if you want the tone to match — its lighting scene (dim the lights for a zone-wide event spot, or brighten the sports book for game time).

Schedule the preset on its own calendar and daypart it: the bar runs happy-hour ads in the late afternoon, the sports book runs game-time ads at tip-off. Each zone's schedule is independent, so one zone's cadence doesn't disturb another.
Repeat for each zone — main floor, bar, lobby — each running its own bank of ads on its own schedule, with its own tone, at the same time.
Walk the floor to confirm each zone is playing what you intended, and adjust the channel, schedule, or lighting from the same panel.
useCases.revert: Each zone can be returned to its standing content by applying that zone's 'normal' preset, or by scheduling it.
assumptions: Each simultaneously-running content stream needs its own player/encoder channel. Confirm the player count recommendation with Mike.

A preset can be scoped to a single venue/zone and can carry a lighting scene alongside content. Confirm the preset UI path for adding lighting, and the lighting processors supported (Mike named ETC Mosaic / Lutron).
useCases.reviewStatus: draft

useCases.title: Build an event campaign that escalates automatically.
useCases.prerequisites: Your event promo asset(s) are loaded in your digital signage CMS and on a signage player → LUCI encoder channel (see UC1 Setup). Confirm whether 'escalation' is a single feature or a preset sequence (see assumptions).
setup: In your digital signage CMS, load the event promo asset(s). For higher frequency closer to the event, build a playlist that rotates the promo more often (or a shorter spot list) — frequency is controlled on the CMS side, zone coverage on the LUCI side.
steps: In LUCI, build a series of presets, each wider than the last: Preset A = one zone (e.g., lobby) on the event channel; Preset B = lobby + concourse; Preset C = full floor on the event channel.
Open the Event Scheduler and place Preset A on the calendar for two weeks out, Preset B for one week out, and Preset C for the week of the event. Each can repeat daily during its window.
To fill slow dayparts between campaign windows, schedule a separate preset that pushes loyalty and dining offers during historically slow windows.
Schedule a 'return to baseline' preset for the day after the event (or set revert times on Preset C) so no stale event content keeps running.
Build it once — the calendar ramps and resets on its own from there.
useCases.revert: A scheduled 'return to baseline' preset the day after the event, plus revert times on the campaign presets, returns the whole floor to normal automatically.
assumptions: Escalation is built as a SEQUENCE of presets on the calendar, not a single 'escalating' feature. Confirm with Mike — LUCI may have a newer campaign/escalation tool not covered in the transcripts.
Frequency (how often the spot plays) is controlled in the CMS playlist, not in LUCI. Confirm.
Zone coverage is controlled in the LUCI preset. Confirm.
useCases.reviewStatus: draft

useCases.title: Set your floor's audio to match the room's energy, all day.
useCases.prerequisites: LUCI open on the property map with your audio zones already on it. Q-SYS is the processor LUCI drives; if you're on Biamp today, LUCI swaps in a Q-SYS processor and reuses your existing amps and sources — confirm the swap with your FDE.
steps: Open LUCI and go to the property map; navigate to the audio zone you want to adjust.
Select the zone's source — which channel or feed plays in that zone — from the source list.
Set the zone's volume. LUCI controls volume per venue, not inside the DSP.

To keep announcements clean, assign mics to priority layers: LUCI's three-layer ducking lets you set security high, page/valley-mic low, and so on — when the high-priority source comes on, it ducks the low.
Adjust the independent volume of each priority per zone (e.g., the restaurant gets security only).
Save the zone's settings; changes apply in real time.
To shift energy by daypart, build a preset that recalls this zone's source and volume (upbeat at night, calm in the morning) and schedule it — see Gaming UC03.
assumptions: Audio control is per-venue source selection + volume + three-layer priority ducking, driven from LUCI (Mike demoed it). Confirm the exact UI path in the current build.
Q-SYS is the primary audio processor LUCI drives. Biamp isn't supported directly — LUCI swaps in a Q-SYS processor and reuses existing amps/sources. Confirm for properties on Biamp.
useCases.reviewStatus: draft — from 04-23 Angel of the Wind demo; confirm audio UI path + Biamp/Q-SYS swap with Mike/Will

useCases.title: Make every jackpot a floor event, automatically.
useCases.prerequisites: LUCI's scripting engine connected to your gaming system so it can listen for progressives and jackpots, and the celebration content (video + audio + lighting scene) loaded as a channel/preset. Confirm the gaming-system integration is wired for your property.
steps: Load the jackpot celebration video as a channel and the celebration sound as an audio WAV in the zone — see Marketing UC01 for getting content into LUCI as a channel.
Create the lighting scene for the celebration on your lighting processor (ETC Mosaic or Lutron); LUCI recalls it by pulling the scenes for that zone.
In LUCI, build a preset that grabs the TVs in the jackpot zone, flips them to the celebration channel, triggers the audio WAV, and recalls the lighting scene — all in one preset.
Connect LUCI's scripting engine to your gaming system so it listens for the jackpot signal.
Set the script to fire the preset the moment a jackpot hits — every TV in the zone flips to the celebration, the sound plays, the lights fire, automatically.
Choose the scope: as mild as one TV, or as wild as every TV, audio zone, and lighting scene in the property.
Optional: set a revert so the floor returns to its baseline after a set time.
assumptions: The scripting engine listens for gaming-system jackpot signals and fires a preset (Mike described it). Confirm the integration is wired today for each property and which gaming systems are supported.
Lighting recall is via ETC Mosaic / Lutron scene recall (Mike named ETC and Lutron). Confirm the processor and scene setup.
Audio WAV trigger from LUCI (Mike described flipping to an audio WAV). Confirm where the WAV is loaded (processor vs. player).
useCases.reviewStatus: draft — from 04-23 Angel of the Wind demo; confirm gaming-system integration + lighting/audio trigger with Mike/Will

useCases.title: Reconfigure the entire property in seconds.
useCases.prerequisites: LUCI open on the property map with the displays, audio zones, and (if used) lighting zones already on it.
steps: Open LUCI and go to the Presets side; click Add and name the preset (e.g., Friday night, Tournament, Morning reset).
Grab the displays you want — a single TV, one venue, or every TV in the property. Use the lasso tool to select many at once on a touchscreen.
For each, set what it should do: change the channel, turn a TV off, set an audio zone's source and volume, recall a lighting scene, even change a video wall's layout.
Add audio and lighting to the same preset if you want — one preset can carry video + audio + lighting + video-wall changes together.
Click Save — the preset populates in the preset list.
Apply it manually any time, or open the Scheduling app and schedule it: set the time, choose daily/weekly/monthly/custom, and save. Everything in the preset recalls at that time.
Optional: set a revert so the property returns to its baseline after a set window — useful for events that should only last an hour.

For the morning reset: build one preset that levels the entire casino (every TV to its baseline channel, every audio zone to baseline volume, lighting to baseline) and schedule it for every morning — no rogue content when the GM walks through.
assumptions: Presets can carry video + audio + lighting + video-wall changes together, and aren't limited in count (Mike demoed it). Confirm the current UI path for adding audio/lighting to a preset.
The lasso tool selects many displays at once on a touchscreen (Mike demoed it). Confirm.
Morning casino reset is a common client preset (Mike described it). Confirm the recommended baseline settings.
useCases.reviewStatus: draft — from 04-23 Angel of the Wind demo; confirm preset/schedule UI + morning reset baseline with Mike/Will

useCases.title: Direct guest attention to a new game area from the moment it opens.
useCases.prerequisites: The new game area's TVs are already on LUCI's map, and you have promo content for the new game loaded as a channel (see Marketing UC01).
steps: Load the new game's promo content as a channel in LUCI (see Marketing UC01 for getting content in as a channel).
Build a preset that grabs the TVs in and around the new game area and flips them to the promo channel — add the zone's audio and a lighting scene if you want the launch to feel like an event.
Open the Scheduling app and schedule the preset to run from the moment the game opens: set the start time, the repeat window, and a revert so the floor returns to baseline after the launch period.
On opening day, the TVs in that area flip to the promo automatically — guests are directed to the new game the moment it goes live, no tap required.
To dial it up for the first weekend, expand the preset to grab more TVs (or the whole property) so the launch gets broader attention, then scale it back once the game is established.
After the launch window, let the preset expire (or delete it) so the floor returns to its normal programming.
assumptions: Directing attention to a new game area uses the same preset + schedule + revert mechanics Mike demoed (drawings/keno to specific TVs at certain hours). Confirm the recommended scope and timing for a launch with Mike/Will.
This use case is composed from the preset/schedule/revert capabilities demoed at Angel of the Wind; it isn't a named feature in the transcript — confirm the framing with Mike.
useCases.reviewStatus: draft — composed from 04-23 Angel of the Wind demo preset/schedule mechanics; confirm launch framing with Mike

useCases.title: Build the whole property's schedule in one session, then let it run.
useCases.prerequisites: LUCI open on the property map with the displays, audio zones, and (if used) lighting zones already on it.
steps: Open LUCI and go to the Presets side. You'll build one preset per mode the property runs — normal weekday, Saturday peak, fight night, holiday, a private event in the ballroom.
For each mode, click Add and name it, then grab the displays and audio zones it covers (use the lasso tool to select many at once on a touchscreen).
Set what each should do at that mode: channel for each TV, source and volume for each audio zone, lighting scene if used, video-wall layout if used.
Save each preset — they populate in the preset list as your library of modes.
Open the Scheduling app and schedule each preset to its daypart: set the time, choose daily/weekly/monthly/custom, and save. Everything in the preset recalls at that time.
Set a locked baseline preset underneath (e.g., the morning reset) so the floor always returns to a known state — the schedule holds the baseline on its own.
To update one piece without disturbing the rest, edit that preset or zone in real time — the change applies live and the rest of the schedule keeps running.
Step back: the whole property now runs itself day to day, and your day shifts from execution to oversight and the occasional adjustment.
assumptions: Building the whole schedule uses the preset + scheduling mechanics Mike demoed (one preset per mode, schedule each to its daypart). Confirm the recommended mode set and baseline with Mike/Will.
Editing one piece in real time without taking the rest offline is how Mike described LUCI's live control. Confirm the exact edit path in the current build.
useCases.reviewStatus: draft — from 04-23 Angel of the Wind demo preset/schedule mechanics; confirm mode set + baseline + live-edit path with Mike/Will

useCases.title: Resolve service requests from wherever you are — including after hours.
useCases.prerequisites: LUCI is browser-based and runs on any device — Safari on iPad, a Surface, even a phone. You can reach it on or off property. Confirm you have remote access to LUCI from your phone.
steps: Get the request — a manager flags that the bar audio is off, or a zone needs a level change.
Open LUCI in the browser on your phone (or tablet) from wherever you are, on or off property.
Go to the property map and navigate to the zone the request is about.
Adjust it: change the source, set the volume, or recall the zone's baseline — the change applies in real time.
Confirm it's right — you can see the zone's live state from the same screen.
Decide whether it really needs an on-site trip. Most level and source issues close from the phone; reserve the walk for genuinely physical problems (a cable, a dead display).
Every change logs itself — you have an automatic record without a separate documentation step.
assumptions: LUCI is browser-based and reactive — works on Safari/iPad, Surface, and phones, reachable on or off property (Mike demoed it). Confirm remote access is enabled for each property's network.
Every change logs itself (Mike referenced logs/monitoring). Confirm what the log captures and where it's reviewed.
useCases.reviewStatus: draft — from 04-23 Angel of the Wind demo (browser-based, any device, remote control, logging); confirm remote access + log scope with Mike/Will

useCases.title: Find problems before guests do.
useCases.prerequisites: LUCI open on the property map. (Live today: per-display online/offline status. The fuller health dashboard and alerting ship in the upcoming release.)
steps: Open LUCI and go to the property map.
Each display shows its status in real time — green means it's on and communicating, red means it's off or not responding.
Scan the map (or a single venue) for any red/offline displays — LUCI knows the moment a TV drops off the network.
Tap an offline display to see its name and start narrowing the cause: a power issue, a network issue, or both.
To get it fixed without a phone call: route the offline status to your ticketing system so the right person is dispatched — or note it and schedule the fix for a quiet window.
Walk in already knowing what needs attention, instead of hearing about it from a guest at the bar.
assumptions: The red/green online/offline indicator is live in the current build (Mike demoed it). Confirm.

Auto-routing offline status to a ticketing system is an integration — Mike phrased it as a capability ('we could take this information and send it to your system to generate a ticket'). Confirm whether it's wired today or part of the upcoming release.
Confirm whether audio-zone and lighting endpoints show the same online/offline indicator, or only video displays.
useCases.reviewStatus: draft — reframed around live offline detection (Ameristar); confirm ticketing-integration status

useCases.title: Configure a private event once, then activate it and let it revert on its own.
useCases.prerequisites: LUCI open on the property map with the displays, audio zones, and (if used) lighting zones for the event space already on it.
steps: Open LUCI and go to the Presets side; click Add and name the preset after the event (e.g., Saturday banquet, Corporate concert).
Grab the displays and audio zones the event uses — the ballroom TVs, the event audio zone, any lighting zones.

Set the full A/V setup in the preset: the custom audio mix (source and volume per zone), the branded screen content (flip the event TVs to the right channel), any zone-specific settings and lighting scene.
Set the revert: enter the number of minutes the event should run before the property returns to its baseline.
Save the preset — it sits in the preset list, ready to reuse for the next instance of the same event.
At event time, activate it with one tap (or schedule it to the event's start time). The preset runs for the event.
When the timer ends, the property returns to its baseline on its own — no tap to switch it off, no risk the floor is left in the event state overnight.
assumptions: The revert function returns everything to its prior state after a set number of minutes (Mike demoed it — 'at the end of that timing, it's going to put everything back exactly the way it was'). Confirm the exact field name for the revert timer in the current build.
Activating a preset is one tap (or a schedule) (Mike demoed it). Confirm the activation path.
useCases.reviewStatus: draft — from 04-23 Angel of the Wind demo (preset + revert function); confirm revert-timer field name + activation path with Mike/Will

useCases.title: Add an endpoint to LUCI — video, audio, or lighting.
useCases.prerequisites: You have an admin PIN and the device's IP address (it must match the field device — the set-top box/TV, the DSP, or the lighting system).
steps: Log in to LUCI with your admin PIN.
Left menu → Administration → Map Modes → Device Setup [Administration].
Select the device type: Video, Audio, or Lighting [Devices]. (On LUCI v2.34.0+, use the Endpoint Manager instead.)
Navigate the map to where the endpoint lives.
Right-click (or long-press) the map → Add Endpoint (for lighting, Add Device).
Video only: pick the Brand from the dropdown. (Audio and lighting skip this.)
Name the endpoint — this is the label shown on the UI.
Notes: add asset tagging or other info you want to track.
Device Address: enter the IP that matches the field device (video: the set-top box/TV; audio: the DSP; lighting: the lighting system).
Assign the endpoint to a Venue so every user on that venue can reach it (unless you restrict it per user — see IT UC03).
Video only: toggle Auto Power to let a watchdog keep the device powered on.
Set any other relevant options, then click Save.
To edit later: right-click the device on the map (or in the Assigned list) → Edit Endpoint.
assumptions: Click-path is the same across video/audio/lighting; only the device-type tab and the IP target differ. Confirm.
v2.34.0+ uses Endpoint Manager — confirm which version the client is on so steps point at the right screen.
Assigning to a Venue gives all venue users access by default; restricting per user is done in User Management → Access (IT UC03). Confirm the linkage.
useCases.reviewStatus: draft — from 3 JSM KB articles (video/audio/lighting endpoint add/edit/remove)

useCases.title: Keep every config, backup, and guide for your system in one place.
useCases.prerequisites: Access to the LUCI Smartsheet and support site — ask your FDE if you don't have credentials yet.
steps: For config and backup files: open the LUCI Smartsheet your FDE shared with you — every config file and backup for your system lives there, fully documented.
For user guides, admin guides, and walkthrough videos: open the LUCI support site.
Before you open a ticket: walk the basic troubleshooting guides on the support site — a lot of issues you can clear yourself.
To report an issue or request a change: file it through the support site's ticketing — no phone tag, no waiting on a vendor.
Reference these any time you need to do something yourself without calling your integrator.
assumptions: Mike says 'we share everything through Smartsheet' — confirm every client is provisioned Smartsheet access by default, or whether it's on request.
Confirm the support site URL and how clients get credentials (ask FDE).
useCases.reviewStatus: draft — from Ameristar transcript (Smartsheet + support site); confirm provisioning with FDE

useCases.title: Define who can change what — by role, by zone, by team.
useCases.prerequisites: You have an admin PIN. The KB article covers per-user source permissions (View/Edit). Confirm with Mike whether zone-level and feature-level access (schedules, health checks) live in this same screen or elsewhere.
steps: Log in to LUCI with your admin PIN.
Navigate to User Management → Access.
Select the user whose access you're setting. Do this before touching any controls — permissions are edited per selected user.
Open the Source tab. You'll see every source in the system and this user's current permission for each.
For each source, set the View permission: Enabled (user can tune a display to it), Disabled (visible in the user's list but can't tune to it), or Hidden (not shown to this user at all).
Set the Edit permission per source: On (user can edit that source's details — edits apply to all users) or Off (read-only for this user).
To set the same permission across every source at once, use the batch controls at the top right: the Options dropdown sets View for all sources, and the Edit All toggle sets Edit for all.
For source-by-source control, use the dropdown and toggle next to each source individually.
Repeat for each user. Permissions take effect immediately.
assumptions: KB covers source-level View/Edit per user. The FAG frames access as 'by role, by zone, by team' — confirm with Mike whether role/zone abstractions exist on top of per-user-per-source, or whether that framing is aspirational.
'Edit On applies for all users of the system' per the KB — confirm source-detail edits are global, not per-user.
Confirm whether non-source permissions (who can edit schedules, run health checks, manage presets) are controlled here or in a separate admin area.
useCases.reviewStatus: draft — from JSM KB article 139427856; needs Mike to confirm role/zone scope

useCases.title: Set up kiosk mode so any staffer can control their area from a phone or mounted touchscreen.
useCases.prerequisites: A small mounted touchscreen (LUCI's ~large-smartphone-sized panel) or any phone with a browser. The venue/zone and the sources you want that kiosk to reach are already on the map.
steps: In LUCI, create a kiosk user (User Management → Access) and assign it a PIN.
Filter that user's access to the venue or zone the kiosk controls, and to just the sources they should pick from (see IT UC03 for access filtering).
Set the user to kiosk mode — list-based control with no map. They get a simple list of displays and channels, not the property map.
Mount the small touchscreen in the space (conference room, cabana, etc.), or have the staffer open the LUCI URL on their phone.
The user logs in with their PIN and lands on a simple list of their displays and channels — tap a display, pick a channel, done.
For a cabana: the guest uses the mounted touchscreen to choose the channel for that cabana's screen — self-serve, no staff involved.
For a conference room: the touchscreen makes it easy to switch between a projector and a flat screen and change the channel.
useCases.revert: n/a — kiosk users persist until changed.
assumptions: Kiosk mode = list-based control without the map (Mike's three user levels: admin, user, kiosk). Confirm the exact toggle/setting name in the current build.
The small touchscreens are LUCI-provided hardware (~large-smartphone-sized) — confirm whether they're included or a separate purchase.
Per-cabana guest self-serve implies a kiosk user per cabana or a shared 'cabana guest' kiosk — confirm the recommended setup with Will/Mike.
useCases.reviewStatus: draft — from 07-14 Cabana/Room/Event Control transcript; confirm kiosk-mode specifics with Will/Mike

useCases.title: Walk the floor with an iPad and take the controls yourself.
useCases.prerequisites: LUCI is browser-based and runs on any device — Safari on iPad works especially well. Confirm you have a login with control of the zones you'll touch.
steps: On your next walkthrough, open LUCI in Safari on the iPad and log in.
Go to the property map and zoom into the area you're standing in — it unnests the individual endpoints so you can see each display and zone around you.
Pick something to change live: flip a screen to a different channel, adjust a zone's audio level, or switch a preset.
Make the change from the iPad — it applies in real time.
Look up from the screen and confirm what LUCI reports matches what you actually see on the floor.
Use the lasso tool to select several displays at once if you want to change a whole section in one gesture.
Repeat through the walk: each live change builds your own fluency so you're not relying on a single operator to read the floor.
assumptions: LUCI is browser-based and reactive on Safari/iPad, with zoom-to-unnest and a lasso tool for multi-select (Mike demoed it). Confirm the GM login has control scope over the zones they'll touch.
This is a fluency/verification use case — the value is the GM seeing and shaping the floor directly. Confirm the recommended walkthrough cadence with Mike.
useCases.reviewStatus: draft — from 04-23 Angel of the Wind demo (browser-based, iPad, zoom/lasso, live control); confirm GM login scope + walkthrough cadence with Mike/Will

useCases.title: Schedule a morning reset so the floor always wakes up looking right.
useCases.prerequisites: LUCI open on the property map with the displays, audio zones, and (if used) lighting zones already on it.
steps: Open LUCI and go to the Presets side; click Add and name it Morning reset.
Grab every display in the property (use the lasso tool, or select-all) and set each to its assigned baseline channel.
Grab every audio zone and set each to its baseline source and volume.
If you use lighting, add the lighting zones and recall the open-of-day scene.
Save the preset — it's now your single source of 'what right looks like' at open.
Open the Scheduling app and schedule the Morning reset to run every day before open (set the time, choose daily, save).
Each morning the floor returns to its baseline on its own — last night's stray changes (a TV on local news, a screen on the wrong input) are erased before anyone checks.
Walk the floor at open and confirm it's correct — then stop running a manual open-of-day checklist.
assumptions: The morning casino reset is a common client preset Mike described — one preset that levels the whole property, scheduled for every morning. Confirm the recommended baseline settings (channels, volumes, lighting scene) with Mike/Will.
Scheduling a preset to run daily before open uses the Scheduling app (Mike demoed it). Confirm the schedule UI in the current build.

useCases.title: Make sure every team is actually using what they can.
useCases.prerequisites: A list of the teams who should be using LUCI (Marketing, Operations, A/V, IT, Finance) and their go-live date. Optional: access to LUCI's logs/usage to see which zones and users are active.
steps: List each function that should be using LUCI and what they're meant to do on it (Marketing: content to every screen; Operations: floor energy and jackpot events; A/V: the property schedule and service requests; IT: endpoints, config, permissions; Finance: the A/V numbers).
For each team, check whether they're actually doing it. Where you can, look at LUCI's logs/usage to see which zones and users have been active since go-live.
Surface where LUCI is sitting idle: is Marketing still routing content through a vendor? Has IT been onboarded to endpoints and permissions? Has Finance revisited the A/V numbers since go-live?
For each stalled team, find the blocker — a missing login, a training gap, a workflow that hasn't been handed over — and unblock it.
Set a date to re-check adoption (e.g., 30 days out) so the investment keeps compounding instead of going to shelfware.
Make it someone's job to close the loop, so 'every team is using what they can' is a standing check, not a one-time push.
assumptions: This is a management/oversight use case — a lightweight adoption audit across teams — not a single LUCI software workflow. It's drafted as a checklist a GM can run.

LUCI has logs/monitoring Mike referenced ('provide logs for all of these players... the basic monitoring'). Confirm whether per-zone/per-user usage is available to support the audit, and what the log shows.
The team-by-team responsibilities map to the other sections' use cases (Marketing, Gaming & Operations, A/V, IT, Finance). Confirm the mapping with Mike.
